solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Phloem)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The vascular bundles of a monocot stem are described as closed.
Reason (R): In a monocot stem, the peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Vascular bundles are closed when there is no cambium between xylem and phloem, as in monocots. The smaller size of the peripheral bundles is a true but separate feature; it does not explain why the bundles are closed.
steps: Bundle size has nothing to do with the absence of cambium
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Monocotyledonous Stem; The Tissue System (Vascular tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (tissue or cell) with List-II (feature).

List-I:
A. Xylem parenchyma
B. Phloem parenchyma
C. Companion cells
D. Spongy parenchyma

List-II:
I. Help in maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes
II. Stores food materials and substances such as resins, latex and mucilage
III. Stores food as starch or fat, and substances such as tannins
IV. Oval or round, loosely arranged cells with large air cavities, extending to the lower epidermis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Living cells of vascular and ground tissues
solution.explanation: Xylem parenchyma stores food as starch or fat and substances like tannins. Phloem parenchyma stores food and substances like resins, latex and mucilage. Companion cells help maintain the pressure gradient in sieve tubes. Spongy parenchyma in a dorsiventral leaf has loosely arranged oval or round cells with large spaces and air cavities.
solution.why_others_wrong: Tannins are linked with xylem parenchyma, and resins, latex and mucilage with phloem parenchyma; the options that swap them are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissues (Xylem; Phloem); Dicotyledonous (Dorsiventral) Leaf
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the anatomy of roots, stems and leaves are correct?

(a) Both dicot and monocot roots have an endodermis and a pericycle.
(b) A monocot stem has a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue.
(c) Monocot roots do not undergo any secondary growth.
(d) In a dorsiventral leaf, the vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thin-walled bundle sheath cells.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Monocot roots, like dicot roots, have epidermis, cortex, endodermis, pericycle, vascular bundles and pith, and they do not undergo any secondary growth. A monocot stem has scattered bundles in a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. In a dorsiventral leaf, the vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick-walled bundle sheath cells.
steps: (d) false: the bundle sheath cells are thick-walled
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', Anatomy of Dicotyledonous and Monocotyledonous Plants
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Medullary rays are a part of the vascular tissue system.
Statement II: In leaves, the ground tissue consists of thin-walled, chloroplast-containing cells called mesophyll.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: All tissues except the epidermis and vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue. In primary stems and roots it includes the cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays. In leaves, the ground tissue is the mesophyll.
steps: Statement I: false, medullary rays belong to the ground tissue system
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Anatomy of Flowering Plants', The Tissue System (Ground tissue system)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Who first saw and described a live cell?

solution.explanation: Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. Robert Brown later discovered the nucleus.
steps: First live cell seen and described → Leeuwenhoek
solution.why_others_wrong: Robert Brown discovered the nucleus. Schleiden contributed to the cell theory. Virchow explained that new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', What is a Cell?
solution.final_answer: Option C: Anton Von Leeuwenhoek

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In green plants, the majority of the chloroplasts are found in the:

solution.explanation: The majority of the chloroplasts of green plants are found in the mesophyll cells of the leaves. They are lens-shaped, oval, spherical, discoid or even ribbon-like organelles.
solution.why_others_wrong: Root cells and root caps are not the main photosynthetic cells, and vessels are dead conducting elements.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Plastids
solution.final_answer: Option A: mesophyll cells of the leaves

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In a prokaryotic cell, several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain. This chain is called a:

solution.explanation: Several ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called polyribosomes or a polysome. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
steps: Many ribosomes on one mRNA → polysome
solution.why_others_wrong: A mesosome is an infolding of the plasma membrane, the nucleoid is the naked genomic DNA region and a plasmid is a small circular DNA outside the genomic DNA.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (Ribosomes and inclusion bodies)
solution.final_answer: Option B: polysome (polyribosome)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A single human cell contains a thread of DNA, distributed among its 46 chromosomes, that is approximately:

solution.concept: Length of DNA in a human cell
solution.explanation: A single human cell has approximately two metre long thread of DNA distributed among its 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).
steps: Human cell: about 2 m of DNA in 46 chromosomes
solution.why_others_wrong: The other lengths are not the NCERT value; they differ by factors of a thousand or more, or by ten.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Nucleus
solution.final_answer: Option D: two metre long

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (cell) with List-II (shape).

List-I:
A. Red blood cell
B. White blood cell
C. Mesophyll cell
D. Nerve cell

List-II:
I. Round and oval
II. Branched and long
III. Round and biconcave
IV. Amoeboid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Cells vary greatly in shape. In the NCERT figure, red blood cells are round and biconcave, white blood cells amoeboid, mesophyll cells round and oval, and nerve cells branched and long.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', An Overview of Cell (Figure: different shapes of cells)
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Matthias Schleiden, who examined a large number of plants, was a British zoologist.
Statement II: Theodore Schwann reported that cells have a thin outer layer, known today as the plasma membrane.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Matthias Schleiden (1838) was a German botanist, and Theodore Schwann (1839) a British zoologist. Schwann reported that cells have a thin outer layer, today known as the plasma membrane, and concluded that the cell wall is a unique character of plant cells.
steps: Statement I: false, Schleiden was a German botanist
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cell Theory
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The cell wall prevents a bacterium from bursting or collapsing.
Reason (R): The bacterial cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides a strong structural support.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides a strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing. R explains A.
steps: Strong structural support → no bursting or collapse → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells (Cell envelope and its modifications)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (description).

List-I:
A. Cilia
B. Flagella
C. Centrosome
D. Microbodies

List-II:
I. Comparatively longer and responsible for cell movement
II. Membrane-bound minute vesicles containing various enzymes, in both plant and animal cells
III. Small structures that work like oars, moving the cell or the surrounding fluid
IV. Usually contains two cylindrical centrioles surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar material

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Cilia are small structures that work like oars, moving the cell or the surrounding fluid; flagella are comparatively longer and responsible for cell movement. The centrosome usually contains two cylindrical centrioles surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar material. Microbodies are membrane-bound minute vesicles containing enzymes, present in plant and animal cells.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Cilia and Flagella; Centrosome and Centrioles; Microbodies
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the endomembrane system are correct?

(a) Camillo Golgi (1898) first observed densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus.
(b) The cis face of the Golgi apparatus is convex and the trans face is concave.
(c) Proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus before they are released from its trans face.
(d) The cis and trans faces of the Golgi apparatus are entirely different and are not interconnected.
(e) The endoplasmic reticulum divides the intracellular space into luminal and extra-luminal compartments.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Camillo Golgi observed the Golgi bodies in 1898. The cisternae have a convex cis (forming) face and a concave trans (maturing) face; the two faces are entirely different but interconnected. Proteins made on the ER are modified in the Golgi cisternae before release from the trans face. The ER divides the intracellular space into luminal (inside ER) and extra-luminal (cytoplasm) compartments.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (a), (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (e).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b), (c) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The number of chloroplasts per cell varies from one per cell in Chlamydomonas, a green alga, to about how many per cell in the mesophyll?

solution.explanation: The number of chloroplasts varies from 1 per cell of Chlamydomonas to 20–40 per cell in the mesophyll.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other ranges are not given by NCERT; they are ten times too small or ten to a hundred times too large.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Plastids
solution.final_answer: Option C: 20 to 40

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing food particles.
Statement II: Lysosomes are rich in hydrolases such as lipases, proteases and carbohydrases, and can digest carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles form by engulfing food particles. Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases) capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Endomembrane System (Lysosomes; Vacuoles)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Mitochondria are easily visible under the light microscope even without specific staining.
Reason (R): Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration and produce cellular energy in the form of ATP.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Mitochondria are not easily visible under the microscope unless specifically stained. They are the sites of aerobic respiration and produce ATP, hence they are called the power houses of the cell.
steps: A: false, they need specific staining to be seen
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Mitochondria
solution.final_answer: Option D: A is false but R is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (size given in NCERT).

List-I:
A. Golgi cisterna (diameter)
B. Chloroplast (length)
C. Prokaryotic ribosome
D. Mitochondrion (length)

List-II:
I. 15 nm by 20 nm
II. 1.0–4.1 µm
III. 0.5 µm to 1.0 µm
IV. 5–10 µm

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Golgi cisternae are 0.5 µm to 1.0 µm in diameter. Chloroplasts are 5–10 µm long and 2–4 µm wide. Prokaryotic ribosomes are about 15 nm by 20 nm. Mitochondria are 0.2–1.0 µm in diameter and 1.0–4.1 µm long.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mitochondria (1.0–4.1 µm long) are shorter than chloroplasts (5–10 µm), and 0.5–1.0 µm is the diameter of a Golgi cisterna; options that swap these values are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells; Golgi apparatus; Mitochondria; Plastids
solution.final_answer: Option B: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about prokaryotic cells are correct?

(a) They are generally smaller and multiply more rapidly than eukaryotic cells.
(b) Plasmid DNA is used to monitor bacterial transformation with foreign DNA.
(c) Their inclusion bodies include phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules and glycogen granules.
(d) Pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein.
(e) The bacterial flagellum has the same structure as the eukaryotic flagellum.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller and multiply faster than eukaryotic cells. Plasmid DNA is used to monitor bacterial transformation with foreign DNA. Inclusion bodies include phosphate, cyanophycean and glycogen granules. Pili are elongated tubular structures of a special protein. Bacterial flagella are structurally different from eukaryotic flagella.
solution.why_others_wrong: (a), (c), (d) and (e) only includes the false statement (e); the three-statement options leave out a true statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Prokaryotic Cells; Cilia and Flagella
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (c) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The cristae increase the surface area of the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Reason (R): Mitochondria divide by fission.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: The inner membrane forms infoldings called cristae towards the matrix, which increase its surface area. Mitochondria also divide by fission. R is a true but separate fact about how mitochondria multiply; it does not explain the role of the cristae.
steps: Division by fission is unrelated to the cristae → not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Mitochondria
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The inner membrane of the chloroplast is relatively less permeable than the outer membrane.
Statement II: Chromoplasts are colourless plastids that store nutrients.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The chloroplast has a double membrane, of which the inner one is relatively less permeable. Chromoplasts contain fat-soluble carotenoid pigments giving yellow, orange or red colours; the colourless plastids that store nutrients are the leucoplasts.
steps: Statement II: false, these are leucoplasts
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Plastids
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the nucleus are correct?

(a) The outer membrane of the nuclear envelope usually remains continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and also bears ribosomes.
(b) The nuclear pores are formed by the fusion of the two membranes of the nuclear envelope.
(c) Every chromosome has a primary constriction, the centromere, on the sides of which lie disc-shaped kinetochores.
(d) Histones, the proteins present in chromatin, are acidic proteins.
(e) The interphase nucleus contains highly condensed chromosomes that are seen as distinct structures.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The outer nuclear membrane is continuous with the ER and bears ribosomes. The nuclear envelope is interrupted by pores formed by fusion of its two membranes. Each chromosome has a centromere with disc-shaped kinetochores on its sides. Chromatin contains DNA and basic proteins called histones. The interphase nucleus has highly extended, elaborate nucleoprotein fibres (chromatin), not condensed chromosomes.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell: The Unit of Life', Nucleus
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: During prophase of mitosis, each centrosome radiates out microtubules called:

solution.explanation: The centrosome, which had duplicated during the S phase, begins to move towards opposite poles in prophase. Each centrosome radiates out microtubules called asters; the two asters together with spindle fibres form the mitotic apparatus.
steps: Centrosome → asters; asters + spindle fibres → mitotic apparatus
solution.why_others_wrong: Kinetochores are disc-shaped structures on the centromere. Chiasmata and the synaptonemal complex belong to prophase I of meiosis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Prophase)
solution.final_answer: Option D: asters

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at metaphase is called the:

solution.explanation: At metaphase, the chromosomes are moved to the spindle equator and aligned there. The plane of alignment of the chromosomes at metaphase is referred to as the metaphase plate.
steps: Plane of alignment at metaphase → metaphase plate
solution.why_others_wrong: The cell plate forms during plant cytokinesis and represents the middle lamella. A furrow forms during animal cytokinesis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Metaphase)
solution.final_answer: Option A: metaphase plate

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: At the time of cytoplasmic division (cytokinesis), which organelles get distributed between the two daughter cells?

solution.explanation: At the time of cytoplasmic division, organelles like mitochondria and plastids get distributed between the two daughter cells.
steps: Cytokinesis: cytoplasm and organelles such as mitochondria and plastids are shared
solution.why_others_wrong: The nucleolus and nuclear envelope reform in telophase; centromeres and kinetochores are parts of chromosomes; asters and spindle fibres form the mitotic apparatus.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Cytokinesis)
solution.final_answer: Option C: Mitochondria and plastids

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Interphase is a period of rest in which the cell neither grows nor replicates its DNA.
Statement II: The M phase starts with cytokinesis and ends with karyokinesis.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Interphase, though called the resting phase, is the time when the cell prepares for division by undergoing both cell growth and DNA replication in an orderly manner. The M phase starts with nuclear division (karyokinesis) and usually ends with division of the cytoplasm (cytokinesis).
steps: Statement I: false, the cell grows and replicates DNA in interphase
Statement II: false, karyokinesis comes first, cytokinesis last
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of cell cycle)
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In plant cells, the new cell wall formed during cytokinesis begins as a simple precursor called the cell plate. The cell plate represents the:

options.text: secondary wall of the daughter cells
middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells
plasma membrane of the daughter cells
nuclear envelope of the daughter nuclei

solution.explanation: In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre and grows outward to meet the lateral walls. It begins with a simple precursor, the cell plate, which represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells.
solution.why_others_wrong: The secondary wall forms later on the inner side of the primary wall; the plasma membrane and nuclear envelope are not formed from the cell plate.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase (Cytokinesis)
solution.final_answer: Option B: middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): A growing cell has to divide to keep its nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio.
Reason (R): Cell growth disturbs the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Cell growth disturbs the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm, so it becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. R explains A.
steps: Growth disturbs the ratio → division restores it → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Significance of Mitosis
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (stage of mitosis) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Prophase
B. Metaphase
C. Anaphase
D. Telophase

List-II:
I. Centromeres split and the chromatids separate
II. The nuclear envelope assembles around the chromosome clusters, and the nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER reform
III. The centrosomes begin to move towards opposite poles of the cell
IV. Its start is marked by the complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: In prophase the duplicated centrosomes begin moving to opposite poles. The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the start of metaphase. In anaphase, centromeres split and chromatids separate. In telophase, the nuclear envelope develops around each chromosome cluster and the nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER reform.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', M Phase
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the later stages of meiosis are correct?

(a) Prophase II is a much simpler prophase than prophase I.
(b) Interkinesis is generally short-lived.
(c) At the end of telophase I, the chromosomes reach the extremely extended state of the interphase nucleus.
(d) In metaphase II, microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids.
(e) In anaphase II, sister chromatids move towards opposite poles by shortening of the microtubules attached to their kinetochores.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: After telophase I, the chromosomes undergo some dispersion but do not reach the extremely extended state of the interphase nucleus. Interkinesis is generally short-lived and is followed by prophase II, a much simpler prophase. In metaphase II, microtubules from opposite poles attach to the kinetochores of sister chromatids; in anaphase II, the centromeres split and the chromatids move apart as the attached microtubules shorten.
steps: (c) false: they do not reach the extended interphase state
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) contain a false statement; (b), (d) and (e) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis (Meiosis I: Telophase I; Meiosis II)
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A plant cell has 2n = 14 chromosomes, and its nucleus contains 2C DNA in the G1 phase. What are the number of chromosomes and the DNA content of this cell in the G2 phase?

solution.concept: DNA content and chromosome number through the cell cycle
solution.explanation: During the S phase, the amount of DNA per cell doubles from 2C to 4C, but there is no increase in the chromosome number: each chromosome now has two sister chromatids. In G2 the cell therefore still has 2n = 14 chromosomes, with 4C DNA.
steps: S phase: DNA doubles, chromosome number unchanged
solution.why_others_wrong: 28 chromosomes doubles the chromosome number, which does not happen in S phase. 2C ignores DNA replication. 7 chromosomes and 2C describes a cell after meiosis I, not a cell in G2.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Cell Cycle (Phases of cell cycle: S phase)
solution.final_answer: Option C: 14 chromosomes and 4C DNA

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Crossing over leads to recombination of genetic material on the two chromosomes.
Reason (R): Crossing over takes place at recombination nodules between the sister chromatids of a chromosome.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In pachytene, recombination nodules appear at the sites where crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes and leads to recombination. R wrongly says sister chromatids.
steps: R: false, crossing over is between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis I (Prophase I: Pachytene)
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In diplotene, the X-shaped structures formed at the sites of crossing over are called recombination nodules.
Statement II: By the end of pachytene, recombination between homologous chromosomes is completed, leaving the chromosomes linked at the sites of crossing over.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: Recombination nodules appear in pachytene at the sites of crossing over, and by the end of pachytene recombination is complete. In diplotene the synaptonemal complex dissolves and the homologues separate except at the sites of crossovers; these X-shaped structures are called chiasmata.
steps: Statement I: false, the X-shaped structures are chiasmata
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Meiosis I (Prophase I)
solution.final_answer: Option D: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A cell with 2n = 10 divides twice by mitosis, every cell dividing once in each round. Each of the cells formed then undergoes meiosis. How many cells are finally formed, and how many chromosomes does each of them have?

solution.explanation: Two rounds of mitosis give 2 × 2 = 4 diploid cells (2n = 10). Each meiosis gives four haploid cells, so 4 × 4 = 16 cells are formed, each with n = 5 chromosomes.
solution.why_others_wrong: 8 cells counts only two products per meiosis. 10 chromosomes forgets that meiosis halves the chromosome number. 32 cells adds an extra doubling.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Mitosis; Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option A: 16 cells, each with 5 chromosomes

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the significance of mitosis and meiosis are correct?

(a) In some lower plants and in some social insects, haploid cells also divide by mitosis.
(b) Meiosis conserves the specific chromosome number of each species across generations in sexually reproducing organisms.
(c) Meiosis takes place during gametogenesis in plants and animals.
(d) Blood cells, which are constantly replaced, arise by meiosis.
(e) Mitosis increases the genetic variability in the population from one generation to the next.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Mitosis is usually restricted to diploid cells, but in some lower plants and some social insects haploid cells also divide mitotically. Mitosis gives genetically identical cells and is used in growth and repair, for example in replacing blood cells. Meiosis occurs during gametogenesis, conserves the chromosome number of the species across generations and increases genetic variability.
steps: (d) false: cell replacement is by mitosis
(e) false: meiosis, not mitosis, increases variability
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Cell Cycle and Cell Division', Significance of Mitosis; Significance of Meiosis
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Within the mesophyll cells, the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls of the cells so that they:

options.text: get the optimum quantity of the incident light
store the maximum amount of starch
come close to the xylem vessels for water

solution.explanation: Photosynthesis takes place in the green parts of the plant, mostly the leaves. Within the mesophyll cells, the chloroplasts generally align themselves along the walls so that they get the optimum quantity of incident light.
steps: Chloroplasts line the mesophyll cell walls → optimum light
solution.why_others_wrong: The alignment is described in relation to light, not to starch storage or water supply.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where does Photosynthesis take place?
solution.final_answer: Option B: get the optimum quantity of the incident light

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In each photosystem, all the pigments except one molecule of chlorophyll a form a light-harvesting system. This system is called the:

solution.explanation: The pigments are organised into two discrete light-harvesting complexes (LHC) within PS I and PS II. In each photosystem, all the pigments except one molecule of chlorophyll a form a light-harvesting system called the antennae. The single chlorophyll a molecule forms the reaction centre.
steps: Antennae: all pigments except one chlorophyll a
solution.why_others_wrong: The reaction centre is the single chlorophyll a molecule. The Z scheme is the shape of the electron carrier sequence. ATP synthase makes ATP.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is Light Reaction?
solution.final_answer: Option D: antennae

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Melvin Calvin found that the first product of CO₂ fixation was a 3-carbon organic acid. His studies used:

solution.explanation: The use of radioactive ¹⁴C by Melvin Calvin in algal photosynthesis studies led to the discovery that the first CO₂ fixation product was a 3-carbon organic acid (PGA).
steps: Calvin: ¹⁴C, algae → first product PGA (3C)
solution.why_others_wrong: NCERT links Calvin's discovery with radioactive carbon, the element being fixed, used in algae.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Primary Acceptor of CO₂
solution.final_answer: Option A: radioactive ¹⁴C in algal photosynthesis

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The concentration of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is very low, between:

solution.concept: CO₂ as a factor in photosynthesis
solution.explanation: Carbon dioxide is the major limiting factor for photosynthesis. Its concentration in the atmosphere is very low, between 0.03 and 0.04 per cent.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other values are ten to a hundred times too high; about 21 per cent is the oxygen content of air.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Carbon dioxide concentration)
solution.final_answer: Option C: 0.03 and 0.04 per cent

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The products of the light reaction are ATP, NADPH and O₂.
Statement II: The O₂ produced in the light reaction is used in the Calvin cycle in the stroma.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The products of the light reaction are ATP, NADPH and O₂. O₂ diffuses out of the chloroplast, while ATP and NADPH are used to drive the processes leading to the synthesis of food (sugars).
steps: Statement II: false, ATP and NADPH (not O₂) are used in the biosynthetic phase
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Where are the ATP and NADPH used?
solution.final_answer: Option C: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The bundle sheath cells of C4 plants have thick walls that are impervious to gaseous exchange and have no intercellular spaces.
Reason (R): The bundle sheath cells of C4 plants are rich in the enzyme RuBisCO.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.concept: Bundle sheath cells of C4 plants
solution.explanation: Bundle sheath cells have a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces. They are also rich in RuBisCO, but this enzyme content says nothing about why their walls are thick or why they lack intercellular spaces.
steps: Enzyme content does not explain wall structure → not the explanation
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (process) with List-II (event).

List-I:
A. Carboxylation
B. Reduction
C. Regeneration
D. Photorespiration

List-II:
I. One ATP is used for phosphorylation to form RuBP
II. RuBP combines with O₂ to form one molecule of PGA and phosphoglycolate
III. RuBisCO fixes CO₂ with RuBP to form two molecules of 3-PGA
IV. Two ATP for phosphorylation and two NADPH for reduction are used per CO₂ fixed

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.concept: Stages of the Calvin cycle and photorespiration
solution.explanation: In carboxylation, RuBisCO fixes CO₂ with RuBP to give two 3-PGA. Reduction uses 2 ATP and 2 NADPH per CO₂ fixed. Regeneration of RuBP uses one ATP. In photorespiration, RuBP binds O₂ to give one PGA and phosphoglycolate.
solution.why_others_wrong: The 3 ATP needed per CO₂ are split as 2 in reduction and 1 in regeneration; options that swap them are wrong.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle; Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option D: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the light reaction are correct?

(a) The pigments are organised into two discrete photochemical light-harvesting complexes (LHC) within Photosystem I and Photosystem II.
(b) Each LHC is made up of hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins.
(c) The reaction centre of each photosystem is made up of several chlorophyll b molecules.
(d) Photophosphorylation is the synthesis of ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate in the presence of light.
(e) Only Photosystem I takes part in non-cyclic photophosphorylation.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The pigments are organised into LHCs within PS I and PS II, each made of hundreds of pigment molecules bound to proteins. The reaction centre is a single chlorophyll a molecule. Photophosphorylation is ATP synthesis from ADP and Pi in light. Both photosystems work in non-cyclic photophosphorylation; only PS I works in cyclic photophosphorylation.
steps: (c) false: the reaction centre is one chlorophyll a molecule
(e) false: both photosystems take part in non-cyclic photophosphorylation
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', What is Light Reaction?; Cyclic and Non-cyclic Photo-phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The overall equation of photosynthesis is
6CO₂ + 12H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6H₂O + 6O₂
and the splitting of water in the light reaction is 2H₂O → 4H⁺ + O₂ + 4e⁻. All the O₂ released comes from water. When two molecules of glucose are made, how many molecules of O₂ are released, and how many molecules of water must be split to release them?

solution.explanation: Each glucose is accompanied by the release of 6 O₂, so two glucose release 12 O₂. Splitting two water molecules gives one O₂, so 12 O₂ require 24 water molecules to be split, which matches 2 × 12 H₂O in the overall equation.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6 O₂ and 12 H₂O is the answer for one glucose. 12 H₂O split assumes one water gives one O₂. 24 O₂ doubles the oxygen released.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Splitting of Water (Light reaction)
solution.final_answer: Option A: 12 O₂; 24 H₂O split

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The temperature optimum for photosynthesis depends on the habitat a plant is adapted to; tropical plants have a higher temperature optimum than plants adapted to temperate climates.
Statement II: An increase in CO₂ concentration up to 0.05 per cent can cause an increase in CO₂ fixation rates, but levels beyond this can become damaging over longer periods.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The temperature optimum depends on the habitat; tropical plants have a higher optimum than temperate plants. Increasing CO₂ up to 0.05 per cent can increase CO₂ fixation, but higher levels can become damaging over longer periods.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Temperature; Carbon dioxide concentration)
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I (molecule) with List-II (number of carbon atoms).

List-I:
A. Ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP)
B. Phosphoglyceric acid (PGA)
C. Oxaloacetic acid (OAA)
D. Glucose

List-II:
I. Six
II. Three
III. Four
IV. Five

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: RuBP, the CO₂ acceptor of the Calvin cycle, is a 5-carbon ketose sugar. PGA, the first product in C3 plants, has three carbons. OAA, the first product in C4 plants, has four. Glucose has six.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Primary Acceptor of CO₂; The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option A: A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Photorespiration is a wasteful process.
Reason (R): In photorespiration, CO₂ is released and ATP is used up.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: In the photorespiratory pathway there is neither synthesis of sugars nor of ATP; instead CO₂ is released and ATP is utilised. Because fixed carbon is lost and energy is spent with no gain, the process is wasteful. R explains A.
steps: Carbon lost + ATP spent → wasteful → R explains A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Photorespiration
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Six turns of the Calvin cycle are required for the removal of one molecule of glucose from the pathway.
Reason (R): Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes six molecules of CO₂.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes one molecule of CO₂. A glucose molecule has six carbons, so the fixation of six CO₂ molecules, that is six turns, is needed to remove one glucose. R is false.
steps: R: false, each turn fixes one CO₂
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Calvin Cycle
solution.final_answer: Option C: A is true but R is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the development of the proton gradient in chloroplasts are correct?

(a) The primary electron acceptor, located towards the outer side of the thylakoid membrane, transfers its electron to an H carrier, which removes a proton from the stroma.
(b) When the H carrier passes its electron to a carrier on the inner side of the membrane, the proton is released into the lumen.
(c) The protons needed to reduce NADP⁺ to NADPH + H⁺ are taken from the lumen.
(d) As a result of these events, the pH in the lumen decreases.
(e) Chemiosmosis requires a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient and ATP synthase.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Protons accumulate in the lumen because (i) water is split on the inner side, (ii) the H carrier removes protons from the stroma and releases them into the lumen, and (iii) NADP reductase on the stroma side uses protons from the stroma. The lumen pH therefore falls. Chemiosmosis needs a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient and ATP synthase.
steps: (c) false: these protons are removed from the stroma
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) contain a false statement; (b), (d) and (e) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The Chemiosmotic Hypothesis
solution.final_answer: Option B: (a), (b), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about C4 plants are correct?

(a) They are adapted to dry tropical regions.
(b) They use the Calvin cycle as the main biosynthetic pathway.
(c) In them, the C4 acid is broken down in the mesophyll cells to release CO₂.
(d) Their bundle sheath cells have a large number of chloroplasts.
(e) In their mesophyll cells, the first stable product of CO₂ fixation is a 3-carbon acid.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: C4 plants are adapted to dry tropical regions. In the mesophyll, PEP is carboxylated to the 4-carbon OAA. The C4 acid moves to the bundle sheath cells, which have many chloroplasts; there it is broken down to release CO₂, which enters the Calvin cycle, the main biosynthetic pathway.
steps: (c) false: the C4 acid is broken down in the bundle sheath cells
(e) false: the first product is the 4-carbon OAA
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (c) or (e) contain a false statement.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', The C4 Pathway
solution.final_answer: Option D: (a), (b) and (d) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A C3 plant and a C4 plant are kept under high light intensity. The CO₂ concentration around them is raised from about 360 µL L⁻¹ to 450 µL L⁻¹. What is expected?

options.text: The rate of photosynthesis of the C4 plant rises, while that of the C3 plant changes little because it is already saturated
The rate of photosynthesis of the C3 plant rises, while that of the C4 plant changes little because it is already near saturation
Neither plant responds, because at high light intensity CO₂ is never limiting
Both plants show a sharp fall in photosynthesis, because any rise above 360 µL L⁻¹ is damaging

solution.concept: Response of C3 and C4 plants to CO₂
solution.explanation: At high light intensities both C3 and C4 plants show an increase in photosynthesis with higher CO₂. C4 plants show saturation at about 360 µL L⁻¹, whereas C3 plants respond to increased CO₂ and saturation is seen only beyond 450 µL L⁻¹. Current CO₂ levels are therefore limiting to C3 plants.
steps: C4 saturates at about 360 µL L⁻¹
C3 saturates only beyond 450 µL L⁻¹
360 → 450 µL L⁻¹: C3 rises, C4 nearly saturated
solution.why_others_wrong: The first option reverses the saturation values. At low, not high, light intensity neither group responds to high CO₂. Damage is described only for levels beyond about 0.05 per cent over long periods.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Photosynthesis in Higher Plants', Factors affecting Photosynthesis (Carbon dioxide concentration)
solution.final_answer: Option B: The rate of photosynthesis of the C3 plant rises, while that of the C4 plant changes little because it is already near saturation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In alcoholic fermentation, pyruvic acid is converted to CO₂ and ethanol by the enzymes:

options.text: pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase

solution.explanation: In fermentation, say by yeast, the incomplete oxidation of glucose is achieved under anaerobic conditions; pyruvic acid is converted to CO₂ and ethanol. The enzymes pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase catalyse these reactions.
steps: Pyruvic acid → (pyruvic acid decarboxylase) → acetaldehyde + CO₂ → (alcohol dehydrogenase) → ethanol
solution.why_others_wrong: Lactate dehydrogenase makes lactic acid. Pyruvic dehydrogenase and citrate synthase work in aerobic respiration in the mitochondria. Invertase acts on sucrose, before glycolysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Fermentation
solution.final_answer: Option B: pyruvic acid decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In respiration, ATP synthesis linked to the electron transport system is called oxidative phosphorylation because the energy used to create the proton gradient comes from:

solution.explanation: Unlike photophosphorylation, where light energy is used to create the proton gradient, in respiration the energy of oxidation-reduction is used for the same process. That is why it is called oxidative phosphorylation.
solution.why_others_wrong: Light energy drives photophosphorylation. GTP hydrolysis and water splitting are not the source of the respiratory proton gradient.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option D: oxidation-reduction reactions

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Fermentation gives a net gain of 2 ATP per molecule of glucose, while complete aerobic respiration can give a net gain of 38 ATP per molecule of glucose. How many molecules of glucose must be fermented to obtain as much ATP as the aerobic respiration of one molecule of glucose?

solution.concept: ATP yield of fermentation and aerobic respiration
solution.explanation: Fermentation gives a net 2 ATP per glucose; aerobic respiration can give a net 38 ATP. Glucose needed = 38 ÷ 2 = 19.
solution.why_others_wrong: 38 forgets that each fermented glucose gives 2 ATP. 76 multiplies instead of dividing. 36 subtracts the 2 ATP of glycolysis instead of dividing.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Fermentation; The Respiratory Balance Sheet
solution.final_answer: Option C: 19

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In aerobic respiration, the complete oxidation of pyruvate takes place in the matrix of the mitochondria, while the passing of electrons to O₂ with the synthesis of ATP takes place on the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Statement II: The oxidative decarboxylation of pyruvic acid requires the participation of several coenzymes, including NAD⁺ and coenzyme A.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

solution.explanation: The complete oxidation of pyruvate by stepwise removal of hydrogen atoms takes place in the matrix, and the transfer of electrons to O₂ with ATP synthesis takes place on the inner membrane. Pyruvic dehydrogenase needs coenzymes including NAD⁺ and coenzyme A.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Aerobic Respiration
solution.final_answer: Option A: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled Assertion (A) and the other is labelled Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Glycolysis is the only process of respiration in anaerobic organisms.
Reason (R): In glycolysis, fructose 1,6-bisphosphate is split into dihydroxyacetone phosphate and 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde (PGAL).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution.explanation: Glycolysis occurs in all living organisms, and in anaerobic organisms it is the only process in respiration. Splitting of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into DHAP and PGAL is a true step of the pathway, but it does not explain why anaerobic organisms depend on glycolysis alone.
steps: R is a step of glycolysis, not the reason for A
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis
solution.final_answer: Option B: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Glycolysis of one molecule of glucose gives a net gain of 2 ATP and forms 2 NADH + H⁺. Assume that this NADH is oxidised through the mitochondrial electron transport system and that each NADH gives 3 ATP. How many ATP are obtained in all from the glycolysis of one molecule of glucose?

solution.concept: ATP from glycolysis under aerobic conditions
solution.explanation: Net ATP made directly in glycolysis = 2. The 2 NADH give 2 × 3 = 6 ATP in the ETS. Total = 2 + 6 = 8.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2 counts only the direct ATP. 6 counts only the NADH. 10 adds the 4 ATP formed directly instead of the net 2 (the 2 ATP used up in glycolysis are not subtracted).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Glycolysis; Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option D: 8

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about respiration are correct?

(a) Respiration is the breaking of C–C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within the cells, leading to the release of considerable energy.
(b) The energy released by oxidation in respiration is used directly by the cell and is not used to synthesise ATP.
(c) Under certain conditions, organic acids can be used as respiratory substrates in some plants.
(d) The carbon skeletons produced during respiration are used as precursors for the biosynthesis of other molecules in the cell.
(e) In the complete combustion of glucose, most of the energy is given out as heat.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: Respiration breaks C–C bonds of complex compounds by oxidation, releasing considerable energy. This energy is not used directly; it is used to synthesise ATP, which is broken down whenever energy is needed. Carbohydrates are the usual substrates, but proteins, fats and even organic acids can be used in some plants under certain conditions. Carbon skeletons from respiration are precursors for biosynthesis. When glucose is burnt completely, most of the energy is given out as heat.
steps: (b) false: the energy is used to synthesise ATP
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (b) contain a false statement; (c), (d) and (e) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Introduction; Do Plants Breathe?
solution.final_answer: Option C: (a), (c), (d) and (e) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the respiratory quotient (RQ) are correct?

(a) The RQ depends upon the type of respiratory substrate used during respiration.
(b) For tripalmitin, 2(C₅₁H₉₈O₆) + 145O₂ → 102CO₂ + 98H₂O + energy, so its RQ is about 0.7.
(c) In living organisms, pure proteins or fats are never used as respiratory substrates.
(d) The RQ of tripalmitin is higher than that of a carbohydrate that is completely oxidised.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The RQ (volume of CO₂ evolved ÷ volume of O₂ consumed) depends on the substrate. For tripalmitin it is 102 ÷ 145 ≈ 0.7, which is lower than the RQ of 1 for a completely oxidised carbohydrate. In living organisms the respiratory substrates are often more than one; pure proteins or fats are never used.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with (d) contain a false statement; (b) and (c) only leaves out the true statement (a).
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Respiratory Quotient
solution.final_answer: Option A: (a), (b) and (c) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
The oxidation of one molecule of pyruvic acid in the mitochondrial matrix (link reaction plus TCA cycle) is summarised as
Pyruvic acid + 4NAD⁺ + FAD⁺ + 2H₂O + ADP + Pi → 3CO₂ + 4NADH + 4H⁺ + FADH₂ + ATP
Taking 3 ATP per NADH and 2 ATP per FADH₂ in the electron transport system, how many ATP are obtained in all from the complete oxidation of the two molecules of pyruvic acid formed from one glucose?

solution.explanation: Per pyruvic acid: 4 NADH × 3 = 12 ATP, 1 FADH₂ × 2 = 2 ATP, and 1 ATP directly (via GTP); total 15. One glucose gives two pyruvic acid molecules, so 2 × 15 = 30 ATP.
solution.why_others_wrong: 15 is the yield of one pyruvic acid only. 28 leaves out the 2 ATP made directly in the cycle. 38 is the total for the whole glucose, including the 8 ATP of glycolysis.
solution.ncert_reference: Class 11 Biology, 'Respiration in Plants', Tricarboxylic Acid Cycle; Electron Transport System (ETS) and Oxidative Phosphorylation
solution.final_answer: Option B: 30

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements about the TCA cycle and the electron transport system are correct?

(a) Continued oxidation of acetyl CoA via the TCA cycle requires the continued replenishment of oxaloacetic acid.
(b) It also requires the regeneration of NAD⁺ and FAD⁺ from NADH and FADH₂.
(c) Oxidation of one molecule of NADH in the electron transport system gives rise to 2 ATP, and of one molecule of FADH₂ to 3 ATP.
(d) In a coupled reaction, GTP is converted to GDP with the simultaneous synthesis of ATP from ADP.
(e) The TCA cycle was elucidated by Hans Krebs.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

solution.explanation: The cycle needs continued replenishment of OAA and regeneration of NAD⁺ and FAD⁺. GTP formed during the conversion of succinyl CoA to succinic acid is converted to GDP with the synthesis of ATP. One NADH gives 3 ATP and one FADH₂ gives 2 ATP. The cycle is also called the Krebs cycle after Hans Krebs, who elucidated it.
